text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.17% today to $140.61, pulling back after hitting a peak of $142.28 on November 13th. The stock has retreated from that high despite oil prices remaining relatively stable—US crude is at $89.62 per barrel and global crude at $92.14—suggesting the move reflects profit-taking or a rotation out of energy stocks rather than a deterioration in the fundamental business backdrop.

The two-week decline of 4.24% follows what appears to have been a rally fueled by the November 11th investment committee discussion of big energy calls on CNBC. With heating oil prices up 59% from last winter and broader energy demand signals still intact (data center electricity growth holding steady), the pullback looks more like normal market volatility after a sharp run-up than a sign of weakening energy fundamentals.
